tagline: Horse carriages and old temples — a town made for slow walks all day
introHtml: Lampang is a northern town that still holds on to its old-time feel. Horse-drawn carriages really do trot through the center, there are old wooden houses along the Wang River, centuries-old temples, and the rooster-bowl pottery the town is famous for. Lately more cafes and younger shops have moved into the old buildings, which makes wandering the old quarter a real pleasure. If you like a town that isn't in a rush and isn't crowded, Lampang is easy to reach and easy to settle into.
bestTime: November–February, cool and comfortable — ideal for walking around town

highlights.name: Lampang horse carriages
highlights.blurb: The only town in Thailand that still runs horse carriages for visitors. A slow ride through the old quarter along the Wang River.

highlights.name: Wat Phra That Lampang Luang
highlights.blurb: The town's iconic old wooden temple, with a golden chedi and an ancient hall. There's a spot where you can see the upside-down reflection of the stupa.

highlights.name: Old town & Kad Kong Ta
highlights.blurb: A riverside walking street along the Wang, lined with old wooden houses and Sino-Burmese buildings. Open weekends, packed with food and stalls.

highlights.name: Rooster bowls
highlights.blurb: The town's signature craft. There are factories and a museum where you can watch them being made, and pick up a rooster-pattern bowl to take home.

highlights.name: Thai Elephant Conservation Center
highlights.blurb: An elephant care center and hospital at Hang Chat. You can see the elephants and learn how they're looked after.

highlights.name: Wat Chaloem Phra Kiat Phrachomklao Rachanusorn
highlights.blurb: White chedis lined up along a limestone ridge — an unusual, striking view. Climb up for a wide sweep of mountains.

foodScene.name: Northern food
foodScene.note: Khao soi, nam ngiao, kaeng hang le, sai ua — easy to find all over town, cooked the proper northern way.

foodScene.name: Khao taen & Lampang treats
foodScene.note: Watermelon-glazed khao taen rice crackers are the town's classic souvenir — crisp, just sweet enough, and easy to carry home.

foodScene.name: Dangling-legs kuay tiao kiao
foodScene.note: An old shop by the Wang River where you sit with your legs hanging over the railing. A local institution worth trying when you're in Lampang.

foodScene.name: Khanom jeen nam ngiao
foodScene.note: Rice noodles topped with northern-style nam ngiao broth, eaten with veggies and pork crackling. Found at markets and morning shops.

foodScene.name: Cafes in old buildings
foodScene.note: The old quarter has plenty of cafes set inside wooden houses and old shophouses — good for a coffee in a retro setting.

foodScene.name: Mu kratha
foodScene.note: A favorite dinner for locals — Thai BBQ hotpot. Lots of places to choose from at easygoing prices.

foodScene.name: Morning markets & street food
foodScene.note: The town markets have rice-and-curry plates, local sweets, and breakfast bites to graze on at local prices.

attractions.name: Wat Phra That Lampang Luang
attractions.blurb: The most beautiful and oldest wooden temple in town, with a golden chedi and the spot for the upside-down stupa reflection.

attractions.name: Kad Kong Ta
attractions.blurb: A walking street in the old quarter by the Wang River — wander past old buildings and graze on snacks on weekend evenings.

attractions.name: Wat Phra Kaeo Don Tao Suchadaram
attractions.blurb: An old temple in the center that once housed the Emerald Buddha, with a golden chedi and a Burmese-style hall to explore.

attractions.name: Wat Chaloem Phra Kiat Phrachomklao Rachanusorn
attractions.blurb: Small white chedis strung along a limestone ridge at Chae Hom — an unusual, lovely view that feels like being up in the hills.

attractions.name: Thai Elephant Conservation Center
attractions.blurb: An elephant care and treatment center at Hang Chat where the whole family can see the elephants and learn about conservation.

attractions.name: Chae Son National Park
attractions.blurb: Natural hot springs and a clear, cool waterfall — soak in the hot water and boil onsen eggs all in one spot.

attractions.name: Baan Sao Nak
attractions.blurb: An old teak house in the center built on hundreds of wooden posts, open to visitors to see its Lanna-Burmese architecture.

attractions.name: Cultural street & Lampang old town
attractions.blurb: A quarter of wooden houses and newer shops tucked into old buildings — fun for a stroll and photos in a retro setting.

itineraryIdeas: Lampang — nature trip to Chae Son hot springs
Lampang — horse carriage ride and temple visits
